style: An illuminated manuscript page — gold-leafed roundels and ink linework on aged parchment, since the article's own imagery (ledgers split into parts, lattices, trellises, rich 'clubs') reads naturally as medieval emblem and diagram.

plates.title: The Spine and the Fan
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page on aged cream parchment, ink linework with gold leaf accents, in a single vertical column of eleven roundels connected by a thin gilded spine running top to bottom, with two scenes (the rich-club citadel, the looping towers, the glowing hill, and the reaching monkey) drawn side by side within a single lightly-bordered enclosure to show they branch from one point and rejoin below. At the top: a brain of threads reaching into a grid of recording probes (RECORDING THOUSANDS OF NEURONS). Below it: twin towers joined by a one-way current from an hourglass to an open gate (PAST FLOWING INTO FUTURE). Next: a river under a bridge where two streams run side by side without mixing (FLOW WITHOUT MIXING). Then a framed region holding FIGURE A as overlapping circles of information beside a scholar's dozen mismatched rulers (A DOZEN RULERS FOR OVERLAP), feeding into a second framed region opening with FIGURE C as a cortical slice on a 512-square grid glowing with recorded points (512 CHANNELS ON A CORTICAL SLICE). From that scene the spine forks into four roundels set in a row: a glowing walled citadel among dim huts (THE RICH CLUB’S SHARE OF SYNERGY); three towers with a bright looping road and a fading dotted feedback path (LOOPS THAT ADD, SIGNALS THAT DON’T); a small hill glowing brightest at its crest (THE PEAK WHERE SYNERGY TURNS TO REDUNDANCY); and a monkey's reaching arm bundled with duplicate glowing threads (REACH-AND-GRASP: REDUNDANCY SURGES). The four roundels converge back onto the spine into a workbench with a tick-comb tool and a smooth-wave lens (DIFFERENT TOOLS FOR DIFFERENT DATA), and finally into a cascade of differently-shaded lights tumbling down a scree slope (AN AVALANCHE WITH CHANGING PROFILES) at the bottom of the page. Palette: faded umber ink, muted blue-green washes, gold leaf for the glowing/synergistic elements. Decorative vine-and-leaf border only at the page edges, kept thin so it never crowds the roundels; each roundel large enough to read clearly, using the full width of the page rather than a narrow central column. No lettering anywhere on the page except the short capitalized titles beneath each roundel exactly as given; no other text, numbers, or inscriptions.

vignettes.quote: electrical and optical recording technologies that can record from hundreds or thousands of neurons
vignettes.depicts: A brain rendered as a hill of fine threads, each thread running to a fine grid of recording probes planted across it like seeds in a field, hundreds of tiny lit points along each thread.

vignettes.quote: the transfer entropy from X’s past to Y’s future
vignettes.depicts: Two neurons drawn as twin towers linked by a single flowing current of ink that runs only one way, from an hourglass marked 'past' at one tower into an open gate marked 'future' at the other.

vignettes.quote: Information transfer captures the overall “flow” of information through the system
vignettes.depicts: A river running beneath a stone bridge where two separate streams meet at the bridge's pillars but pass under side by side without mixing, showing flow without any blending of the two currents.

vignettes.quote: There are, at present, close to a dozen competing redundancy functions
vignettes.depicts: FIGURE A redrawn as an illuminated roundel of overlapping circles of shared information, set beside a dozen different measuring rulers of unequal length laid out by a scholar, none agreeing with the others.

vignettes.quote: 512-channel multielectrode arrays to record hundreds of individual neurons in vitro from organotypic cultures derived from mouse cortical slices
vignettes.depicts: FIGURE C redrawn as a thin sagittal slice of cortex laid upon a fine 512-square grid plate, with hundreds of small glowing dots scattered across the slice where neurons are recorded.

vignettes.quote: triads with two recurrent connections and no feedback connections had 50% more synergy
vignettes.depicts: Three linked towers where a looping road circles back between two of them (bright and glowing) while a dotted path running back from the third tower fades to nothing.

vignettes.quote: The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value
vignettes.depicts: A small hill on the map glowing brightest exactly at its crest, with the slope dimming both toward the flat ground below and toward a steeper far slope beyond the peak.

vignettes.quote: during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically
vignettes.depicts: A monkey's arm reaching to grasp an object, with many duplicate glowing threads bundled together running from the head down to the hand, far more copies than along the arm's resting threads.

vignettes.quote: binary, spiking data, the relevant redundancy function will be different from when attempting to analyze largely Gaussian fMRI-BOLD data
vignettes.depicts: A workbench holding two different instruments side by side: a comb-like tool counting sharp on/off ticks, and a smooth curved lens for a soft rolling wave, neither usable for the other's material.

vignettes.quote: neuronal avalanches (a common signature of complex, critical dynamics in the nervous system) have distinct “computational profiles”
vignettes.depicts: A cascade of small lights tumbling down a slope like a scree-fall, each tumbling light a different shade from the one before it, showing the fall changing in character as it descends.

plates.title: Splitting the Ledger
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, ink and gold leaf on aged parchment, arranged as eight roundels in a single descending chain linked by a thin gilded vine, read top to bottom. At the top, framing the chamber: FIGURE A as overlapping circles of information beside a dozen mismatched rulers (A DOZEN RULERS FOR OVERLAP). Below it, a neuron at a fork between a lit lightning-bolt path and a dark path, threads feeding in without simply summing (TO FIRE OR NOT TO FIRE). Next, a neuron as a weaver's loom crossing colored threads into a new pattern (WEAVING INPUTS INTO COMPUTATION). Then two scholars dividing one pile of coins into smaller labeled piles with quill and ruler (SPLITTING THE LEDGER INTO PARTS). Next, FIGURE A again, now with a lone figure's telescope trained on a single circle, lighting only the sliver visible there (WHAT ONLY ONE SOURCE REVEALS). Then a locksmith turning one key while three other locks on a chain spring open by themselves (ONE KEY, THREE LOCKS SPRING FREE). Then FIGURE B redrawn as a wildly branching trellis beside a short tally-stick with only a few notches (ATOMS OUTGROWING KNOWN TERMS). Finally, at the bottom, a gardener's trellis with one fruit hanging at a high crossed junction, unreachable from any lower branch (FRUIT NOT FOUND ON LOWER BRANCHES). Palette: faded umber and soft sepia ink, restrained gold leaf on the lit/illuminated elements (lightning bolt, telescope's circle, open locks, high fruit), muted green for vines and trellises. A thin decorative vine border at the page edges only, never crowding the roundels — each roundel large and legible, spanning most of the page's width. No lettering anywhere except the short capitalized titles beneath each roundel exactly as given; no other words, numbers, or inscriptions appear on the page.

vignettes.quote: There are, at present, close to a dozen competing redundancy functions
vignettes.depicts: The same opening image as the overview's framework scene: FIGURE A as overlapping circles of information beside a scholar's dozen mismatched rulers, framing the chamber this plate opens into.
vignettes.title: A DOZEN RULERS FOR OVERLAP

vignettes.quote: whether to fire an action potential or not
vignettes.depicts: A single neuron at a fork in the road, one path lit by a small lightning bolt and the other dark, with many thin threads from parent neurons feeding into the fork but not simply adding together.
vignettes.title: TO FIRE OR NOT TO FIRE

vignettes.quote: the target neuron can be thought of as performing a kind of integrating “computation”
vignettes.depicts: A neuron drawn as a weaver's loom, many colored threads from different sources crossing and interlacing into a new woven pattern on the loom's frame.
vignettes.title: WEAVING INPUTS INTO COMPUTATION

vignettes.quote: it was recognized how to algebraically decompose the total joint mutual information into the particular contributions of the parts
vignettes.depicts: Two scholars at a ledger, dividing one large pile of coins into several smaller labeled piles with a quill and ruler, the whole sum exactly accounted for among the smaller piles.
vignettes.title: SPLITTING THE LEDGER INTO PARTS

vignettes.quote: the information about Y that could only be learned by observing Xᵢ
vignettes.depicts: FIGURE A redrawn with a lone figure holding a telescope trained only on one circle of the diagram, seeing a sliver that is lit only there and nowhere else in the overlapping circles.
vignettes.title: WHAT ONLY ONE SOURCE REVEALS

vignettes.quote: If any of the unknown terms can be defined, then the other three emerge “for free”.
vignettes.depicts: A locksmith turning one key in a single lock, and three other locks on a chain springing open on their own the moment the first turns.
vignettes.title: ONE KEY, THREE LOCKS SPRING FREE

vignettes.quote: the number of distinct partial information atoms grows much faster than the number of known mutual information terms
vignettes.depicts: FIGURE B redrawn as a trellis branching wildly into many small fruiting knots, set beside a short tally-stick with only a few notches, showing the trellis far outgrowing the tally.
vignettes.title: ATOMS OUTGROWING KNOWN TERMS

vignettes.quote: information that is not accessible in any simpler combination of sources lower down on the lattice
vignettes.depicts: A gardener's trellis with a single fruit hanging at a high, particular junction of crossed vines, a fruit that cannot be reached by climbing any of the lower, simpler branches of the trellis.
vignettes.title: FRUIT NOT FOUND ON LOWER BRANCHES

plates.title: What the Recordings Showed
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, ink and gold leaf on aged parchment, arranged as seven roundels: the first stands alone at the top as a frame, then three roundels sit side by side in a row sharing one border beneath it, then the chain continues downward through two more roundels to a final scene. At the top: FIGURE C as a cortical slice on a glowing 512-square grid (512 CHANNELS ON A CORTICAL SLICE), opening the chamber. Below it, a single vessel pours a stream of ink into a smaller vessel that always fills to a quarter of the larger one's level (A QUARTER OF THE FLOW BECOMES SYNERGY), from which the chain forks into three side-by-side roundels: a glowing walled citadel among dim huts (THE RICH CLUB’S SHARE OF SYNERGY); three towers with a bright looping road and a fading dotted path (LOOPS THAT ADD, SIGNALS THAT DON’T); and a small hill glowing brightest at its crest (THE PEAK WHERE SYNERGY TURNS TO REDUNDANCY). The three converge back into a cartographer drawing a bridge far wider than the actual ford beneath it (A BRIDGE MEASURED TOO WIDE), and finally into a monkey's reaching arm bundled with duplicate glowing threads (REACH-AND-GRASP: REDUNDANCY SURGES) at the bottom. Palette: faded umber and sepia ink, muted blue-green washes, gold leaf reserved for the glowing/synergy elements (grid points, citadel, hill-crest, looping road). A thin vine-and-leaf border only at the page's outer edge, kept narrow so it never crowds the roundels; each roundel drawn large and legible, using the full width of the page. No lettering anywhere on the page except the short capitalized titles beneath each roundel exactly as given; no other words, numbers, or inscriptions appear.

vignettes.quote: 512-channel multielectrode arrays to record hundreds of individual neurons in vitro from organotypic cultures derived from mouse cortical slices
vignettes.depicts: FIGURE C redrawn as a thin sagittal slice of cortex laid upon a fine 512-square grid plate, with hundreds of small glowing dots scattered across the slice where neurons are recorded, the same scene opening the overview's rich-club chamber.

vignettes.quote: synergy observed in a given triad was reliably about a quarter of the transfer entropy for that triad
vignettes.depicts: FIGURE D's scatter panel redrawn as a stream of ink pouring from a vessel labeled by its flow into a smaller vessel, the smaller vessel always filling to exactly one quarter of the larger one's level.

vignettes.quote: triads with two recurrent connections and no feedback connections had 50% more synergy
vignettes.depicts: FIGURE D's connectivity panel redrawn as three linked towers with a bright looping road circling back between two of them, and a dotted path running back from the third tower fading to nothing.

vignettes.quote: The peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value
vignettes.depicts: FIGURE D's timescale panels redrawn as a small hill glowing brightest exactly at its crest, dimming toward flat ground on one side and a steeper far slope on the other.

vignettes.quote: bivariate analyses overestimate the significance of bivariate edges
vignettes.depicts: A cartographer hunched over a map, drawing a bridge between two towns far wider and thicker than the narrow ford actually crossing the river beneath it.

vignettes.quote: during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically
vignettes.depicts: A monkey's arm reaching to grasp an object, with many duplicate glowing threads bundled together running from the head down to the hand, far more copies than along the arm's resting threads.
